posts.subject: External Monitor Flickers When Connected to Legion Pro 7 16IAX10H via HDMI Cable
posts.author: danielmit
posts.message_html:
Hello,

I recently bought a Legion Pro 7 16IAX10H. The way I use this laptop is by connecting it to my monitor via an HDMI 2.1 cable. The issue I am having is that on boot, and while gaming, the external monitor constantly flickers on and off as if its gaining, then losing connection, then gaining and losing again.

I have tried using a different monitor, as well as switching HDMI cables, but this did not work leading me to conclude that the issue must be with the laptop. I was wondering if anyone has experienced this and has been able to resolve this?

posts.subject: Re:External Monitor Flickers When Connected to Legion Pro 7 16IAX10H via HDMI Cable
posts.author: Hassen_Lenovo
posts.message_html:
Hi danielmit,

Thank you for reaching out to the Lenovo Community regarding your Legion Pro 7 16IAX10H and the external monitor flickering issue. Does the flicker happen only during boot and gaming, or also during normal desktop use?

I’m sorry that you are having this issue, and I know how frustrating it can be when your external monitor keeps flickering despite trying different cables and monitors. Since you’ve already ruled out the cable and monitor, the problem is most likely tied to HDMI handshake or driver/firmware settings on the laptop.

Here are some steps worth trying:

  • Update BIOS, chipset, and GPU drivers through Lenovo Vantage → System Update.

  • In NVIDIA Control Panel, set the external monitor to a stable refresh rate (for example 60Hz or 120Hz) and disable G‑Sync if enabled, as HDMI handshake can fail with variable refresh.

  • Test with a certified HDMI 2.1 cable shorter than 2m, as longer cables sometimes cause intermittent signal drops.

  • If your monitor supports DisplayPort or USB‑C input, try connecting that way to confirm whether the issue is HDMI‑specific.

  • In Windows Display Settings, disable “Dynamic refresh rate” and set a fixed refresh rate to reduce flicker.

If the flicker only happens during boot but stabilizes afterward, it may be a firmware quirk. If it persists during gaming, it’s more likely a driver/handshake issue.

Best regards, Hassen_Lenovo

posts.subject: Re:External Monitor Flickers When Connected to Legion Pro 7 16IAX10H via HDMI Cable
posts.author: danielmit
posts.message_html:
Hey Hassen,

thank you for the response. To address your point/ask follow up questions:

Update BIOS, chipset, and GPU drivers through Lenovo Vantage → System Update.

I did and my system is completely up to date.


In NVIDIA Control Panel, set the external monitor to a stable refresh rate (for example 60Hz or 120Hz) and disable G‑Sync if enabled, as HDMI handshake can fail with variable refresh.

In NVIDIA Control Panel my external monitor is set to a 240Hz refresh rate, however Windows Display Settings says its 239.76Hz. G-Sync is also disabled.

Test with a certified HDMI 2.1 cable shorter than 2m, as longer cables sometimes cause intermittent signal drops.

My HDMI 2.1 cable is 4 feet long, so it's well under 2m.


If your monitor supports DisplayPort or USB‑C input, try connecting that way to confirm whether the issue is HDMI‑specific.

When I use an HDMI to USB-C/Thunderbolt adapter and plug it into my computer's USB-C port, everything runs well and there is no flickering.


In Windows Display Settings, disable “Dynamic refresh rate” and set a fixed refresh rate to reduce flicker.

Dynamic Refresh Rate is disabled, however as previously stated, my Windows Display Settings for this monitor does not allow for a 240Hz option, instead giving me only 239.76Hz

Based on what you have said it seems that the last part with Windows Display Settings only allowing 239.76Hz, while NVIDIA Control Panel shows 240Hz is what's causing the issue? Would the fix here be to set both to 120Hz since that is what is equally available?

Although it does feel kind of bad not using my monitor to its full refresh rate capacity... Look forward to hearing from you.
